messages:
incident-bot: PAGER -> acmecorp-private-vpc: GPU queue growth >95% for 12m. Autoscaler failing to provision new nodes (errors: volume-attach timeout, image pull 429). Paging current oncall.

emily: I'm oncall, looking.

emily: Quick snapshot: gateway shows ~12k queued tokens, 82% of GPU pool in use, backend enqueue latency spiking. Autoscaler logs show repeated 'nodeProvisionRateLimit' and 'preflight: storage-attach timeout' entries.

emily: Running basic checks now:
```
kubectl -n acme get pods -l app=gpu-worker -o wide
kubectl -n acme describe pod <pending-pod>
```

raj: I see ~14 Pending pods with reason=PodScheduled->FailedAttachVolume then kubelet not registering. A few nodes stuck in bootstrap (kubelet never reported Ready).

maya: Is this the cluster with the custom disk/ephemeral-image config? Last week the same account hit slow image pulls because their NAT gateway egress is throttled.

liam: If boot is slow + imagepulls are 429ing, autoscaler keeps retrying but cooldown/cap prevents burst. Two quick mitigations: increase autoscaler max temporarily (10->20) or manually add a transient node pool using ondemand images.

emily: I'll try manual node injection. Creating a warm pool now:
```
# internal infra tool
infractl nodepool create --cluster acmecorp --machine g4dn.xlarge --count 8 --labels temp-autoscale-override=true
```

infra-bot: request accepted -> creating nodepool p-87c3. Expected ready in ~6m.

emily: Also bumping node boot timeout on this cluster to 25m and disabling join drain to speed registration.

raj: note: even if nodes appear, imagepulls might still fail if registry is rate-limited. Pre-pulling or using a mirror will help.

maya: Customer uses a small NAT IP pool with limited bandwidth to the public registry. I can ping SE to request temporary egress or mirror.

emily: Pinging SE now @maya. Also switching routing for a portion of traffic to hosted fallback as a stopgap.
```
routectl set-traffic --customer acmecorp --percent-hosted 30
```

ops: Routing change applied: 30% traffic diverted to hosted (us-west2). Watching queue metrics.

emily: infra-bot reports nodepool p-87c3 ready: 7 nodes Registered, 1 initializing.

raj: Pods are scheduling onto new nodes but some show ImagePullBackOff. I'll try pre-pull via mirror on those nodes.

maya: SE replied: customer can open egress to registry for 20 minutes, enabling faster pulls. They enabled it.

liam: Good. Once images pull, pods should stabilize. We should still treat this as degraded until queue back to normal. Root cause hypothesis: autoscaler hitting a chain failure (volume attach timeouts + imagepull 429) causing scale loop and conservative cooldown preventing sufficient burst.

emily: Confirming partial mitigation: queue dropping from 12k tokens to ~3k after routing + new nodes, but some workloads still backlogged. Marking customer-impact as "degraded" -> "partial mitigation".

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS update: mitigated -> impact reduced, pager escalations paused.

emily: Next steps to fully remediate: 1) add registry/mirror check into autoscaler preflight 2) relax autoscaler cooldown and add occasional burst allowance for customer profiles with slow boot 3) run a capacity test for acmecorp VPC profile and document NAT egress guidance.

raj: I'll collect and upload logs for postmortem. DRI: raj. Uploaded logs to internal storage: /incidents/1715004321/logs.tar.gz (link posted in #incidents attachments).

emily: Handoff to daytime oncall @liam for follow-ups, customer comms, and postmortem.

liam: Copy. I'll take ownership of the postmortem and coordinate a fix (autoscaler preflight + burst policy). Will loop in infra and devex.

emily: :thumbsup:
